BiblicalUsage: The brandishing of a sword is the flash of it before it falls, and Ezekiel uses this word once, in the song of the sword. In Ezekiel 21:15 the sword is sharpened to make a sore slaughter, furbished that it may glitter, and the prophet cries that it is pointed against their gates.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the glitter of the sword is meant to frighten before it cuts: God warned Jerusalem first, and the warning itself was mercy.
